gross-efficiency.short: Mechanical power ÷ metabolic power. In cycling about 20%: the rest of the energy becomes heat.

heat-balance.short: S = M − W − R − C − K − E: heat stored equals metabolic energy minus external work minus heat lost by radiation, convection, conduction and evaporation.

heat-storage.short: The part of the heat produced that is not lost. Positive storage warms the body; zero storage means body temperature holds steady.

convection.short: Heat carried away by moving air or water flowing past the skin. More airflow, more heat lost, as long as the air is cooler than the skin.

thermal-radiation.short: Heat passed as infrared waves between surfaces that don't touch. The sun and hot tarmac give heat to you; you give heat to cooler surroundings.

conduction.short: Heat passed by direct contact between surfaces, such as skin on a saddle or an ice vest. Usually a tiny part of exercise heat exchange.

evaporative-heat-loss.short: Heat taken from the skin when sweat turns to vapour. The main way to lose heat during hard exercise, and the only one when the air is hotter than the skin.

latent-heat.short: The energy needed to turn a liquid into vapour without changing its temperature. For sweat, about 2.4 kJ per gram evaporated.

sweating-efficiency.short: The fraction of the sweat produced that actually evaporates. Sweat that drips off or soaks into clothing cools little or not at all.

skin-wettedness.short: How much of the skin must be wet with sweat to lose the heat needed. Above about half, sweat starts to drip and cooling per gram falls.

core-temperature.short: The temperature deep in the body (blood, organs, brain), about 37 °C at rest. Measured in the rectum, oesophagus or gut.

prescriptive-zone.short: The range of climates in which core temperature during steady exercise depends on work rate, not on air temperature. Above it, the climate pushes core temperature up.

balance-point.short: The core temperature the body defends. Classic models call it a set point; newer models see it as the level where several separate heat-loss and heat-gain loops balance.

skin-blood-flow.short: Blood sent to the skin to carry heat from the core to the surface. In the heat it can take several litres per minute away from muscle and heart filling.

hyperthermia.short: A core temperature above normal because heat gain beats heat loss, as in hard exercise in the heat. Unlike fever, the defended temperature has not moved.

wbgt.short: A heat-stress index for the environment: 0.7 × natural wet bulb + 0.2 × black globe + 0.1 × dry air temperature. It ignores the athlete's heat production and clothing.

ingestible-sensor.short: A pill-sized radio thermometer swallowed a few hours before exercise; it reads gut temperature as it passes through, a practical field measure of core temperature.
